complete.problem: In scene s3, follow the magnets as a worked example: the south pole of one magnet faces the north pole of the other, so the opposite poles attract and the loose magnet slides across and snaps onto the first with a click. Each step is a check: read the pole labels, decide whether the facing poles are opposite or the same, then predict attract or repel before the magnets move.

steps.text: Step 1: Opposite poles attract: every magnet has a north pole and a south pole, and when S faces N the magnets pull together and snap with a click.
steps.annotation: The two ends of a magnet, marked N and S: opposite poles attract and like poles repel.

steps.text: Step 2: Read the pole labels first, then decide whether the facing poles are opposite or the same: S faces N, so the facing poles are opposite.
steps.annotation: Read the pole labels first, then decide whether the facing poles are opposite or the same.

steps.text: Step 3: Opposite poles attract, so the loose magnet slides across and snaps onto the first with a click.
steps.annotation: What opposite poles do: a north pole and a south pole facing each other pull together and snap onto each other.

complete.selfExplanation: Explain in one sentence why you must read the pole labels before predicting whether two magnets will attract or repel.

faded.problem: The south pole of one magnet is brought near the north pole of another magnet. What happens, and why?

steps.text: Step 1: read the pole labels: the south pole of one magnet faces the north pole of the other.
steps.annotation: The two ends of a magnet, marked N and S: opposite poles attract and like poles repel.

steps.text: Step 2: S and N are opposite poles, so opposite poles attract.
steps.annotation: Scene s3: opposite poles attract - when S faces N the magnets pull each other and snap together with a click.

steps.text: Step 3: so the magnets pull together and snap onto each other.
steps.annotation: They attract: the magnets pull together and snap onto each other.

faded.selfExplanation: The first step is shown. Say what happens to the two magnets, and why.

paired.problem: Two magnets are brought together with their north poles facing each other. What happens?
paired.solution: They push each other apart and repel
